messages:
kai: FYI incoming from monitoring — customer Frostline on dedicated pool dedicated-us-west-2-3 started getting 429s after a sudden traffic jump ~09:12 UTC. Alerts show tps spiked to ~240 and stayed high for ~2m. Customer sees repeated "rate_limited" errors. Ticket #SUP-34567. Can oncall pick up?

anika: oncall here, can you paste any request IDs and a short log slice? also which model variant were they pinned to?

kai: quick paste from proxy logs (request IDs redacted):
```
[09:12:07] admission_controller: account=frostline requested_tps=246 limit_tps=200 burst_credits=0 decision=reject reason=burst_credits_depleted
[09:12:07] proxy: upstream=generator-1 latency=12.3ms status=200
[09:12:08] proxy: admission_queue: size=48 avg_wait_ms=320
[09:12:09] auth: token_check ok account=frostline
[09:12:10] proxy: respond status=429 body={"error":"rate_limited"} request_id=REDACTED
```
Model pinned: redwood/gpt-medium-8k:q8_0 (no auto-fallback configured).

matt: looking at infra metrics — autoscaler did not add instances because pool already at max_reserved=8 and scale policy requires sustained cpu>60% for 60s. GPUs were ~55% at peak due to KV cache churn; request queueing increased but autoscaler threshold never tripped. Also saw large spike in token decoding time for that model during the window (per-token latency up ~2x).

laura: billing note — ledger shows Frostline's burst credit balance was 0 at 09:11:30. We received a billing ingestion delay for allocations between 09:00–09:10; that may have prevented automatic top-up. I've opened a billing subtask.

sre-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: SUP-34567 — 429 spike for account=frostline (dedicated-us-west-2-3). Pinged oncall.

anika: repro checklist so eng can iterate locally:
1) set account header `x-account-id: frostline`
2) hit `/v1/generate` with concurrency 30 and requests that request ~1k tokens per call (seq len 1024).
3) use quick loop for 2m to emulate burst.
Sample curl loop:```bash
for i in {1..60}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "x-account-id: frostline" -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium-8k:q8_0","prompt":"x","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & done; wait
```
Capture `admission_controller` logs and `proxy` queue depth.

kai: mitigation we applied: temporarily routed Frostline traffic to dedicated-us-west-2-5 (same instance type) and manually granted a one-off burst credit of 5000 tokens via internal billing API to restore traffic. Customer reported decreased 429s after ~30s.

matt: proposed root-cause hypothesis: 1) billing ingestion lag left account without credits during spike; 2) admission control uses a conservative per-second token budget with no soft-fallthrough when credits are zero; 3) autoscaler gating by sustained CPU prevented quick scale at short high-concurrency bursts because per-GPU utilization metric undercounts queued inference time. Together caused early rejections before new capacity could spin up.

anika: suggested fixes (short-term and long-term):
- short-term: implement a short-duration emergency headroom reserve per pool (10–20% reserved capacity) that admission can draw from when account credits are temporarily missing (configurable per-account).
- short-term: allow admission to prefer model-fallback (to smaller quantized variant) instead of hard reject when burst_credits==0.
- medium-term: change autoscaler to consider queue_depth and avg_wait_ms as scale signals (not just GPU util).
- medium-term: add a grace path for billing ingestion delays: if ledger update lag > 30s, treat account credits as last-known-positive for an additional 60s.

laura: +1 on grace for billing. Also request we add an audit column in billing events to track which top-ups were delayed and why. I'll own follow-up with finance.

kai: can someone take ownership for the incident postmortem and remediation checklist? We should include: repro steps, exact log excerpts, autoscaler tuning proposal, admission policy patch, and rollback plan.

matt: I'll own the autoscaler side and run a small canary change that scales on queue_depth > 40 for 15s. I'll instrument a dashboard.

anika: I'll file an eng task for admission fallback + emergency headroom feature with PR template and spec.

laura: I will reconcile the manual burst grant with billing and issue a compensatory credit if needed.

kai: thanks all — customer updated that errors dropped to <1% after routing and manual credit. Marking SUP-34567 as under investigation. Assigning follow-ups: ENG-AUTO (matt), ENG-ADMIT (anika), FIN-BILL (laura). Ping if anything new shows up. :thumbsup:
